questions.fact: It was the first NFL title game decided in sudden-death overtime, and millions watched on TV.

questions.question: Bill Mazeroski's home run won the 1960 World Series for Pittsburgh. Which team did they beat?
questions.fact: It was the first time a World Series ended on a home run.

questions.question: Which team was Wilt Chamberlain playing for when he scored 100 points in 1962?
questions.fact: That same season he averaged over 50 points a game, still an NBA record.

questions.question: Which Dodgers pitcher dominated the Yankees as Los Angeles swept the 1963 World Series?
questions.fact: He struck out 15 Yankees in Game 1, a World Series record at the time.

questions.question: Cassius Clay became heavyweight champion in February 1964 by beating which fighter?
questions.fact: He was a big underdog. Soon after, he announced his new name, Muhammad Ali.

questions.question: Which Australian swimmer won the women's 100 meter freestyle at three Olympics in a row, starting in 1956?
questions.fact: She won in Melbourne in 1956, Rome in 1960 and Tokyo in 1964.

questions.question: Floyd Patterson became the youngest heavyweight champion in 1956. How old was he?
questions.fact: He was also the first heavyweight champion to win the title back after losing it, in 1960.

questions.question: The Milwaukee Braves beat the Yankees in the 1957 World Series. Which pitcher won three games?
questions.fact: He threw three complete-game wins, two of them shutouts.

questions.question: In the 1958 World Series, the Yankees got revenge on which team that had beaten them the year before?
questions.fact: New York came back from three games to one down to win.

questions.question: In 1959, the newly moved Los Angeles Dodgers won the World Series. Which team did they beat?
questions.fact: Game crowds at the giant Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum topped 92,000.

questions.question: The new American Football League played its first season in 1960. Which team won its first title?
questions.fact: The AFL later merged with the NFL, and the rivalry gave birth to the Super Bowl.

questions.question: Which American won the decathlon at the 1960 Rome Olympics?
questions.fact: In 1984 he lit the Olympic flame at the opening of the Los Angeles Games.

questions.question: The Yankees won the 1961 World Series. Which team did they defeat?
questions.fact: Whitey Ford ran his streak of scoreless World Series innings to a record 32.

questions.question: Which American swimmer won four gold medals at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics?
questions.fact: He was 18 and won both freestyle sprints plus two relays.

questions.question: Which fiery St. Louis pitcher beat the Yankees in Game 7 of the 1964 World Series?
questions.fact: He was named Most Valuable Player of the Series.

questions.question: What were golfer Arnold Palmer's huge, loyal crowds of fans called?
questions.fact: He won the first of his four Masters titles in 1958.

questions.question: Which 17-year-old Brazilian star helped his country win the 1958 World Cup?
questions.fact: He scored twice in the final against Sweden.

questions.question: Which Yankee center fielder won baseball's Triple Crown in 1956?
questions.fact: He led the league in batting average, home runs and runs batted in, with 52 home runs.

questions.question: In 1958, the New York Giants baseball team moved to which city?
questions.fact: Their old rivals, the Brooklyn Dodgers, moved to Los Angeles the very same year.

questions.question: In 1958, the Brooklyn Dodgers began playing in which city?
questions.fact: Until Dodger Stadium was ready, they played in the huge Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

questions.question: Which Boston Celtics center won 11 championships, the first in 1957?
questions.fact: The NBA Finals Most Valuable Player award is now named after him.

questions.question: Which sprinter, who wore a leg brace as a child after polio, won three gold medals at the 1960 Olympics?
questions.fact: She was called 'the fastest woman in the world.'

questions.question: Which golfer, who won his first major in 1962, was nicknamed 'the Golden Bear'?
questions.fact: He beat Arnold Palmer in a playoff to win the 1962 U.S. Open.

questions.question: Which TV sports show, starting in 1961, promised 'the thrill of victory… and the agony of defeat'?
questions.fact: Jim McKay hosted it for decades on ABC.

questions.question: In 1961, Yankee sluggers Mickey Mantle and Roger Maris were nicknamed what?
questions.fact: They chased Babe Ruth's home run record together all summer.

questions.question: In 1957, which tennis player became the first Black champion at Wimbledon?
questions.fact: She won Wimbledon and the U.S. title in both 1957 and 1958, and later played pro golf too.

questions.question: Soon after winning the heavyweight title in 1964, Cassius Clay changed his name to what?
questions.fact: He became one of the most famous people in the world, in sports and beyond.

questions.question: Which Chicago Black Hawks star of the early 1960s was nicknamed 'the Golden Jet'?
questions.fact: He was famous for his blazing slap shot, and helped Chicago win the Stanley Cup in 1961.

questions.question: The brand-new New York Mets of 1962 set a record for what?
questions.fact: They lost 120 games. Their manager was 72-year-old Casey Stengel.

questions.question: What did Ted Williams do in the very last at-bat of his career, in 1960?
questions.fact: He would not tip his cap to the cheering Fenway Park crowd. Writer John Updike wrote a famous story about the day.

questions.question: Which jockey, nicknamed 'The Shoe,' stood under five feet tall and won thousands of races?
questions.fact: He won the Kentucky Derby four times, the first in 1955 aboard Swaps.

questions.question: The Pro Football Hall of Fame opened in 1963 in which Ohio city?
questions.fact: The NFL was founded in Canton in 1920.

questions.question: Abebe Bikila of Ethiopia won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome. What was unusual about how he ran?
questions.fact: He became the first Black African to win an Olympic gold medal. He won the marathon again in 1964.

questions.question: Which player, nicknamed 'the Big O,' averaged a triple-double for a whole NBA season in 1961–62?
questions.fact: That means he averaged double figures in points, rebounds and assists. No one did it again for 55 years.

questions.question: Northern Dancer won the 1964 Kentucky Derby. Which country was he from?
questions.fact: He became one of the most important sires in racing history.

questions.question: Which little-known golfer stunned Ben Hogan to win the 1955 U.S. Open?
questions.fact: He beat Hogan in an 18-hole playoff, using clubs made by Hogan's own company.

questions.question: Which San Francisco Giants pitcher was famous for his sky-high leg kick?
questions.fact: He was nicknamed 'the Dominican Dandy.' He threw a no-hitter in 1963.

questions.question: Which Green Bay Packers star was nicknamed 'the Golden Boy'?
questions.fact: He ran, caught passes and kicked, and set an NFL scoring record in 1960.

questions.question: Maury Wills of the Dodgers set a record in 1962 by stealing how many bases?
questions.fact: He broke the modern record set by Ty Cobb back in 1915, and was named National League MVP.

questions.question: Who won the very first Daytona 500, in 1959, after a photo finish?
questions.fact: It took NASCAR three days of studying photos to declare him the winner. His son Richard later won the race seven times.

questions.question: In 1961, which South African became the first golfer from outside the US to win the Masters?
questions.fact: He was nicknamed 'the Black Knight' because he often dressed all in black.

questions.question: Which Green Bay quarterback led the Packers to five NFL titles in the 1960s?
questions.fact: He was also named MVP of the first two Super Bowls.

questions.question: In 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on a city bus. In which city did this happen?
questions.fact: Her quiet stand led to a bus boycott that lasted 381 days.

questions.question: Which young minister rose to fame leading the Montgomery bus boycott, starting in 1955?
questions.fact: He was just 26 years old and pastor of a church in Montgomery, Alabama.

questions.question: In 1957, the Soviet Union launched the world's first satellite. What was it called?
questions.fact: It was a shiny metal ball only 58 centimeters (about 23 inches) across, and its radio beeps could be picked up on Earth.

questions.question: After Alaska and Hawaii became states in 1959, how many stars did the American flag have?
questions.fact: The 50-star flag became official on July 4, 1960, the first Independence Day after Hawaii joined.

questions.question: Which country sent the first human into space, in 1961?
questions.fact: Yuri Gagarin made one orbit of the Earth and became a hero around the world.

questions.question: In 1961, a wall was built splitting a famous German city in two. Which city?
questions.fact: It stood for 28 years, until joyful crowds began tearing it down in November 1989.

questions.question: Which famous speech did Martin Luther King Jr. give at the March on Washington in 1963?
questions.fact: He spoke from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial.

questions.question: Which president signed the Civil Rights Act into law in 1964?
questions.fact: He signed it on July 2, 1964, with civil rights leaders gathered around him.

questions.question: Disneyland opened in July 1955 in which California city?
questions.fact: Opening day had so many problems, from melting asphalt to broken rides, that staff called it 'Black Sunday.'

questions.question: President Eisenhower signed a 1956 law that created what?
questions.fact: He had been impressed by Germany's autobahns. The system is officially named after him.

questions.question: In 1957, nine Black students bravely integrated Central High School in Little Rock. Which state is that in?
questions.fact: They became known as the Little Rock Nine. President Eisenhower sent soldiers to escort them to class.

questions.question: NASA was created in 1958 mainly in response to which Soviet success?
questions.fact: NASA officially opened for business on October 1, 1958.

questions.question: Cuba, where Fidel Castro took power in 1959, lies about how far from Key West, Florida?
questions.fact: On a clear night, Cuban radio stations could be heard in Florida.

questions.question: Vice President Nixon and Soviet leader Khrushchev had a famous 1959 argument in a model of which room?
questions.fact: It happened at an American exhibition in Moscow, and became known as the 'Kitchen Debate.'

questions.question: How old was John F. Kennedy when he was elected president in 1960?
questions.fact: He was the youngest person ever elected president, and the first Catholic.

questions.question: In 1962, John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth. How many times did he go around?
questions.fact: His capsule was named Friendship 7. He returned to space at age 77 in 1998.

questions.question: Rachel Carson's 1962 book 'Silent Spring' warned about the dangers of what?
questions.fact: It helped lead to a US ban on the pesticide DDT and to the modern environmental movement.

questions.question: About how many people attended the 1963 March on Washington?
questions.fact: It was one of the largest gatherings for civil rights in American history.

questions.question: The 1957 Treaty of Rome created the European Common Market. How many countries signed it?
questions.fact: They were Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.

questions.question: America's first satellite, Explorer 1, made a big discovery in 1958. What did it find?
questions.fact: They were named the Van Allen belts, after the scientist whose instruments found them.

questions.question: The Antarctic Treaty, signed in 1959, set Antarctica aside for what?
questions.fact: It was first signed by 12 countries. Military activity there is banned.

questions.question: Kennedy beat Nixon in 1960 by about what share of the popular vote?
questions.fact: He won by about 112,000 votes out of almost 69 million cast.

questions.question: Seventeen African nations gained independence in 1960. What is that year often called?
questions.fact: Most of the new nations had been French colonies.

questions.question: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961. About how long did his flight last?
questions.fact: As he blasted off he called out 'Poyekhali!', Russian for 'Let's go!'

questions.question: Which became the 49th state in January 1959?
questions.fact: It is by far the largest state. The US had bought it from Russia in 1867.

questions.question: Which volunteer program, sending Americans to help in other countries, did President Kennedy start in 1961?
questions.fact: Volunteers taught school, built wells and helped on farms around the world.

questions.question: Which First Lady gave the country a televised tour of the newly restored White House in 1962?
questions.fact: More than 80 million viewers watched her show off the $2 million restoration with CBS reporter Charles Collingwood.

questions.question: How many digits were in the new ZIP codes the Post Office introduced in 1963?
questions.fact: A cartoon mailman named Mr. ZIP helped teach people to use them.

questions.question: Which tower was built for the 1962 World's Fair in Seattle?
questions.fact: The fair was called the Century 21 Exposition, and it looked ahead to life in the future.

questions.question: What happened to Elvis Presley in March 1958 that made headlines everywhere?
options: He was drafted into the Army
questions.fact: News cameras filmed his famous Army haircut. He served in West Germany.

questions.question: Which Ford car of 1958 became a famous flop?
questions.fact: It was named after Henry Ford's son Edsel. Its name became a byword for a failure.

questions.question: Finish Kennedy's 1961 line: 'Ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for…'
questions.fact: He said it in his inaugural address on a snowy January day in Washington.

questions.question: In 1963, Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union became the first woman to do what?
questions.fact: She orbited the Earth 48 times in nearly three days aboard Vostok 6.

questions.question: Which Soviet leader complained during his 1959 US visit that he wasn't allowed to go to Disneyland?
questions.fact: Officials said they couldn't guarantee his safety there. He visited a farm in Iowa instead.

questions.question: In 1964, the Surgeon General's famous report warned Americans about the health dangers of what?
questions.fact: It was released on a Saturday in January 1964 to limit the effect on the stock market.

questions.question: In January 1961, Ham went into space and came back safely. What was Ham?
questions.fact: He was trained to pull levers when lights flashed, and he did his job well. He lived for another 22 years.

questions.question: What giant steel globe was the symbol of the 1964 New York World's Fair?
questions.fact: It is 12 stories high and still stands in Flushing Meadows, Queens.

questions.question: Which waterway, opened in 1959 by the US and Canada, let ocean ships sail from the Atlantic into the Great Lakes?
questions.fact: Queen Elizabeth II and President Eisenhower took part in the opening ceremonies.

questions.question: TIROS-1, launched in 1960, was the first successful satellite of what kind?
questions.fact: It sent back the first television pictures of Earth's clouds from space.

questions.question: In 1959, NASA introduced its first group of astronauts. How many were there?
questions.fact: They were called the Mercury Seven and included Alan Shepard and John Glenn.

questions.question: In 1955, America's two biggest labor groups joined together. What was the new group called?
questions.fact: George Meany became its first president.

questions.question: Which pope, elected in 1958, called the Second Vatican Council?
questions.fact: He was 76 when elected, and is still fondly remembered as 'the Good Pope.'

questions.question: Which World War II French leader became president of France in 1959?
questions.fact: He founded France's Fifth Republic. The main Paris airport is named after him.

questions.question: President Eisenhower beat the same Democrat in both 1952 and 1956. Who was he?
questions.fact: He was the governor of Illinois and later served as ambassador to the United Nations.

questions.question: In 1957, a copy of which famous ship sailed from England to Plymouth, Massachusetts?
questions.fact: It left Plymouth, England, in April 1957 and got a ticker-tape parade in New York. Visitors can still tour it today.

questions.question: In 1964, which Maine senator became the first woman to seek the Republican nomination for president?
questions.fact: She served in both the House and the Senate, and was the first woman elected to both.

questions.question: Comedian Vaughn Meader's best-selling 1962 album poked fun at which family?
questions.fact: It was called 'The First Family,' and it won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year.

questions.question: In 1958, Pan Am began jet service across the Atlantic with which new Boeing airliner?
questions.fact: Jets cut the trip from New York to Europe to about seven or eight hours.

questions.question: The first full-scale nuclear power plant in the US began making electricity in 1957 in which state?
questions.fact: It was at Shippingport, near Pittsburgh.

questions.question: The 23rd Amendment, ratified in 1961, gave voters in which place the right to vote for president?
questions.fact: D.C. residents first voted for president in the 1964 election.

questions.question: Movie star Grace Kelly married a real prince in 1956. Which country's royal family did she join?
questions.fact: She married Prince Rainier III and became Princess Grace. She gave up acting for good.

questions.question: Dr. Seuss published 'The Cat in the Hat' in 1957. What colors is the Cat's tall hat?
questions.fact: Dr. Seuss used only 236 different words, so beginning readers could read it on their own.

questions.question: Which toy craze of 1958 had kids swiveling their hips to keep a plastic ring spinning?
questions.fact: An inventor saw children in Australia playing with bamboo hoops, and Wham-O began selling a plastic version in 1958.

questions.question: The Barbie doll first went on sale in 1959. Which toy company made her?
questions.fact: Ruth Handler created Barbie and named her after her daughter, Barbara.

questions.question: In early 1960s slang, if something was 'a drag,' what was it?
questions.fact: 'What a drag!' was a favorite teenage groan when plans fell through.

questions.question: In early 1960s slang, what did 'Far out!' mean?
questions.fact: It started with jazz and beatnik fans and later became a favorite of the hippies.

questions.question: In 1964, G.I. Joe was introduced as a boys' version of which hugely popular doll?
questions.fact: Hasbro never called him a doll. They invented the term 'action figure' instead.

questions.question: Ray Kroc opened his first McDonald's in 1955. How much was a hamburger?
questions.fact: His restaurant was in Des Plaines, Illinois. Fries cost a dime.

questions.question: What did 'keeping up with the Joneses' mean in the 1950s suburbs?
questions.fact: The phrase came from a newspaper comic strip that started in 1913.

questions.question: In 1958, the price of a first-class stamp went up from 3 cents to what?
questions.fact: It was the first increase in 26 years. The price went up again, to 5 cents, in 1963.

questions.question: Jack Kerouac's 1957 novel 'On the Road' became the bible of which group?
questions.fact: He typed the first draft on one long scroll of taped-together paper.

questions.question: In late 1950s hip talk, if you needed some 'bread,' what were you short of?
questions.fact: 'Dough' had meant money for years, so 'bread' was a short hop away.

questions.question: In mid-1960s teen slang, if a new car was 'boss,' what was it?
questions.fact: Ford even named a famous high-powered Mustang the 'Boss.'

questions.question: In 1956, the federal minimum wage went up to how much an hour?
questions.fact: President Eisenhower signed the raise into law in August 1955, and it took effect the next year.

questions.question: Betty Friedan's 1963 best seller about the lives of American housewives was called 'The Feminine…' what?
questions.fact: She called the unhappiness of many educated homemakers 'the problem that has no name.'

questions.question: About how much did the new Ford Mustang cost when it came out in April 1964?
questions.fact: Its advertised list price was $2,368. Ford built it on the parts of its plain, economical Falcon to keep the price low.

questions.question: Which squishy modeling dough for children was first made as a wallpaper cleaner?
questions.fact: It was sold to schools as a toy starting in 1956, and its smell is still famous.

questions.question: Which red drawing toy with two white knobs became a Christmas hit in 1960?
questions.fact: You shook it upside down to erase the picture.

questions.question: Which flying plastic disc did the Wham-O company start selling in 1957?
questions.fact: It was first sold as the 'Pluto Platter,' cashing in on the craze for flying saucers.

questions.question: What did the original Easy-Bake Oven of 1963 use to bake its tiny cakes?
questions.fact: Kenner made it, and it came in turquoise or yellow.

questions.question: At a 1950s drive-in movie, where did the sound come from?
options: A speaker hung on your car window
questions.fact: Drive-ins hit their peak in the late 1950s, with about 4,000 across the country.

questions.question: Which big Burger King sandwich was introduced in 1957?
questions.fact: It sold for 37 cents when it first came out.

questions.question: Which towering 1960s hairdo was named after the home of a busy insect?
questions.fact: It was created in 1960 by Chicago hairdresser Margaret Vinci Heldt, and needed lots of hairspray.

questions.question: Which toaster pastries first came out in 1964?
questions.fact: Kellogg's made them. The first ones had no frosting.

questions.question: In cereal ads from 1959 on, the kids told a rabbit: 'Silly rabbit, ___ are for kids!'
questions.fact: The poor rabbit almost never got to eat any.

questions.question: Which 1960 Mattel doll talked when you pulled the string in her back?
questions.fact: She said 11 phrases at random, like 'I love you' and 'Please take me with you.'

questions.question: What was the name of Barbie's boyfriend, introduced in 1961?
questions.fact: He was named after Ruth Handler's son, Kenneth.

questions.question: Which wet backyard toy did Wham-O start selling in 1961?
questions.fact: It was a long plastic sheet that you sprayed with a garden hose and slid across on your belly.

questions.question: Which bald, muscular cleaning mascot first appeared in 1958?
questions.fact: Procter & Gamble introduced him, and his catchy jingle helped sales take off.

questions.question: Which orange drink powder came out in 1959 and later went into space with astronauts?
questions.fact: Sales were slow until NASA used it on John Glenn's 1962 flight.

questions.question: Which board game, first made in 1860, was relaunched by Milton Bradley in 1960 with a spinning wheel and little cars?
questions.fact: Players fill their little plastic cars with pegs as they marry and have children along the way.

questions.question: In 1962, Sam Walton opened his first Walmart in which Arkansas town?
questions.fact: He had already been running Ben Franklin variety stores in Arkansas for years.

questions.question: In 1963, the Bell System began offering which new kind of telephone?
questions.fact: The Touch-Tone phone replaced the rotary dial, and later added the * and # keys.

questions.question: Zenith's 'Space Command' of 1956 was one of the first wireless what?
questions.fact: It used sound you couldn't hear. Pressing a button struck a tiny metal rod inside, so people called it a 'clicker.'

questions.question: Bank of America's charge card, launched in 1958, later became which famous card?
questions.fact: It was called BankAmericard and was first tested by mailing cards to people in Fresno, California.

questions.question: Which tiny brine shrimp, sold through comic book ads, became a popular 'instant pet'?
questions.fact: Inventor Harold von Braunhut first sold them in 1957 as 'Instant Life.'

questions.question: The first Pizza Hut opened in 1958 in which Kansas city?
questions.fact: Two college-age brothers, Dan and Frank Carney, borrowed $600 from their mother to start it.

questions.question: Which slippery coating came to American kitchens on frying pans in the early 1960s?
questions.fact: The first nonstick pan sold in America was called 'The Happy Pan.'

questions.question: Which toothpaste, launched in 1955, was one of the first with fluoride to fight cavities?
questions.fact: In 1960 it became the first toothpaste approved by the American Dental Association.

questions.question: Which diet group was started in 1963 by a New York homemaker, Jean Nidetch?
questions.fact: It began as weekly meetings of friends in her home in Queens.

questions.question: Which sugar substitute in pink packets was introduced in 1957?
questions.fact: It was created by a Brooklyn father and son who ran a cafeteria across from the Navy Yard.

questions.question: Converse's canvas basketball sneakers, a 1950s teen favorite, were named after which man?
questions.fact: Teenagers called them 'Chucks,' and they came in high-tops and low-tops.

questions.question: In the early 1960s, what new invention let you open a can of soda or beer without an opener?
questions.fact: Ermal Fraze came up with it after he forgot his can opener and had to open a beer on a car bumper.

questions.question: Which wild-haired little dolls from Denmark became a fad in America in the early 1960s?
questions.fact: A Danish woodcarver, Thomas Dam, made the first ones, starting in 1959.

questions.question: The Xerox 914, introduced in 1959, was the first popular office machine that could do what?
questions.fact: It was so popular that 'to Xerox' became an everyday word for making a copy.

questions.question: Which boxed rice dish, launched in 1958, was sold as 'the San Francisco treat'?
questions.fact: It was made by the Golden Grain Macaroni Company of San Francisco.

questions.question: Which two-seat Ford sports car first went on sale in 1955?
questions.fact: Ford called it a 'personal luxury car,' not a sports car, to set it apart from the Corvette.

questions.question: Which lemon-lime soda did the Coca-Cola Company launch in the US in 1961?
questions.fact: It was created to compete with 7 Up. It had started in West Germany in 1959 as Fanta Klare Zitrone.

questions.question: Velcro was patented in 1955. What gave its Swiss inventor the idea?
questions.fact: George de Mestral spent years working out how to copy the tiny hooks that made burrs cling to fur.

questions.question: What was the very first Barbie doll of 1959 wearing?
questions.fact: She came as a blonde or a brunette, with her hair in a ponytail.
